page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance engineered for heavily threaded, compute-intensive workloads. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the virtual server provides 96 vCPUs mapped across 48 physical execution cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 256 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 2.67 GB per virtual core. Local persistence is supplied via a dedicated 1280 GB NVMe SSD array, while baseline networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational capabilities alongside stable single-threaded throughput. In synthetic CPU stress tests, the multi-core stress-ng metric places within the top ten percent of all tested platforms, corroborated by top-tier PassMark results in physics simulation, encryption, and extended vector instructions. Highly parallel developer workloads also benefit directly from the dense core count, as evidenced by top-quartile performance in Clang software compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects the modest 2.0 GHz base frequency, producing middle-tier Geekbench single-core figures and below-average single-threaded gzip compression rates.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high compute density per dollar, making it advantageous for horizontally scaled or multi-process pipelines that fully saturate 96 cores without needing vast memory per thread. The local 1280 GB NVMe storage avoids the latency penalties of remote volumes, although memory-intensive deployments with high per-thread footprints may face capacity limits. Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is well matched for continuous integration build farms, parallel batch processing, distributed data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency caching tiers such as Redis.
description: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by dedicated 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC hardware configured with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) and 256 GB of RAM. The instance includes 1280 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and excludes dedicated GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks highlight outstanding multi-core compute capability, with top-tier results in multi-threaded stress-ng metrics, PassMark encryption, and physics calculations, alongside strong Clang compilation and multi-threaded decompression throughput. Single-core performance falls into the middle tier, reflecting its parallel core density over high single-threaded clock frequencies. Memory bandwidth remains solid for cached blocks, and the platform delivers over 100 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. This server profile suits parallel CI/CD compilation, distributed data processing, ray tracing, and compute-heavy batch workloads.
